text: State what is meant by ‘reliability’.
Explain the difference between ‘qualitative data’ and ‘quantitative data’.

parts.text:
The participants in this study were all male. A new experiment could explore gender differences
in the effect of epinephrine. However, the stooge may influence emotions differently in males
and females.
Suggest how a difference between the influence of the stooge on males and females could
affect the results about gender differences in the effect of epinephrine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A second new experiment could include a stooge who claims to feel ill because of the
injection.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest how one participant variable could affect the results of this second new
experiment.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain one ethical problem with this second new experiment.

parts.text:
Explain why each of these problems affected the validity of this study.
the task involved a forced choice between only two response options ______
the test included basic mental states ______

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain how solving one of these problems improved the validity of the eyes test.

text: In the study by Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test), eight problems of validity were identified with the
original version of the eyes test. Two of these problems were that:
• the task involved a forced choice between only two response options (the two words
presented)
• the test included basic mental states.
In the study by Milgram (obedience), the sample included a range of occupations.
Name two of these occupations.
Describe the use of ‘open questions’ and ‘closed questions’ in research, using any examples.

Geoffrey finds that the time participants spend on social media is normally distributed.

their use of social media further.

parts.text:

text: Geoffrey is conducting structured interviews about people’s use of social media. He is investigating

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Faolan asks each teacher to rate how annoyed they feel when a student in their class
doodles.
Suggest a scale that Faolan could use to measure how annoyed the teachers are.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain one problem with the scale that you have suggested in (a)(i), including how this
would affect the results.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Faolan is interested to know whether teachers show the same behaviours in the classroom
when students doodle as they reported during the interview.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest two reasons why the teachers’ interview responses may differ from their
behaviour in the classroom. Your answers should not relate to the scale you suggested
in (a)(i).

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
If Faolan finds that teachers do not show the same behaviours in the classroom as they
report during the interview, this raises an ethical issue.
Suggest why it could be difficult for Faolan to follow the ethical guideline of ‘protection
from harm’ when she explains her results to the participants.

text: Faolan is investigating teachers’ attitudes and behaviours towards students doodling. She has
conducted a semi-structured interview and has observed the teachers in the classroom.

parts.text:

Explain how one ethical guideline relating to animals would affect her decision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Tulip is finding a median. She puts her scores in order.
State what a researcher should do to find the median if there are two middle numbers.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain how Tulip would find the range of the number of sociable behaviours of the animals in
the small cage.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Explain why it would be appropriate for Tulip to use counterbalancing if she chose a repeated
measures experimental design.

text: Tulip is conducting a study on social behaviour in animals. She is investigating whether animals
are more sociable when they are in a large laboratory cage or a small laboratory cage.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Enfys could conduct a natural experiment to investigate whether some types
of shopper are more relaxed than other types of shoppers. You may choose to compare
shoppers with trolleys/carts and baskets or any other different types of shopper.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.
